story_title: As Venue Staff, I want to review a venue booking request so that I can decide whether the requested venue can be made available for the event

acceptance_criteria.text: Venue Staff can view pending booking requests.
The request displays the requested venue, date, time and event information.
Venue Staff can approve the request.
Venue Staff can reject the request.
Venue Staff can provide a reason when rejecting a request.
Venue Staff can suggest an alternative venue or arrangement when rejecting a request, for the Coordinator to review and act on.
An approved booking request becomes a Confirmed booking — the same status referenced by Detect Venue Booking Conflicts and View Venue Availability.

open_questions: RESOLVED 2026-10-02 (Kayal): the booking's badge reads 'Approved', as in the BPMN (docs/ConnectSphere_BPMN.drawio, gateway 'Booking approved?' -> 'approved'). AC7's 'Confirmed booking' is that approved booking: the stored status is 'approved', which the availability calendar (SPM-46) shows as 'Booked' and conflict detection (SPM-44) blocks on (TC03, TC04). 'Confirmed' stays an event status only ('Confirm event' is the Coordinator's later step in both diagrams), so a booking is never labelled 'Confirmed'.

RESOLVED 2026-09-18 (Kristen, Jira comment on SPM-43): notifying the Coordinator of the outcome is out of scope - notifications belong to SPM-53. No test case covers a notification, and the decision route writes none (removed 2026-10-02). The Coordinator finds the decision, reason and suggestion on the event's Venue tab (TC03, TC08, TC09, TC10).

RESOLVED 2026-10-02 (Kayal): the suggestion is an optional venue picker plus an optional free-text 'Alternative arrangement'. It is a suggestion only - nothing is booked or requested (customer #45, #110); the Coordinator submits a new request, which SPM-42 already tests.
RESOLVED 2026-10-02: a refusal whose request has left the list (SPM-43-TC12, decided in another tab) is shown at the top of the Booking Requests page instead of on the card.

RESOLVED 2026-10-02 (Kayal): approval blocked by an unavailable venue and by a retired venue are tested by hand (TC13, TC14), each on its own test venue so no other tester's data is touched. Venue Staff can retire and restore a venue in the app, so TC14 does both itself. Recording an unavailability period has no screen yet (Block venue, S-23 - DOCUMENTATION.md Known Gaps), so TC13's period is created by the fixture script.

RESOLVED 2026-10-03 (Kayal): a pending request whose event is still Submitted or Under review is not listed on Booking Requests (TC15) - Venue Staff could not approve it, so showing it would only be noise. It joins the list once the event is approved. SPM-54 stops such a request being made, so this only covers requests that already exist; the server also refuses to approve one, which no screen can reach, so no case tests that refusal by hand (unit tested).

Reverting: a case that approves or rejects says so in its Preconditions ('This case changes data: run npm run fixtures:spm43 once when you finish testing …'). That command is the only reset needed and is never a reseed - it resets only the 'SPM43 …' events in place (their booking requests and decisions are dropped and recreated; each event keeps its EVT- reference), makes 'SPM43 Retire Test Room' active again and resets 'SPM43 Maintenance Room' to its one maintenance period. Nothing outside the SPM43 test data is changed by any case.

Fixtures: scripts/seed-spm43.ts creates fourteen 'SPM43 …' events in May 2027, on base-seed venues plus the two test venues SPM43-MNT and SPM43-RET; prisma/seed.ts creates the same rows. Each event keeps its EVT- reference between runs on one database, but the number differs from one database to another, so the cases name events by title and never ask the tester to type an event address.
